title: RES↔FW-001: Research Algorithm Transfer + Firmware Feasibility Assessment
description: The Researcher provides research-grade PoC (Proof-of-Concept) firmware, algorithm specifications (signal-processing steps, calibration procedures, sensor-fusion logic), scientific rationale for design choices, and preprocessing specifications with a Python golden reference and test vectors; the Firmware Engineer provides a firmware-feasibility assessment (estimated CPU cycles, Flash/SRAM budget impact, peripheral conflicts, RTOS compatibility, real-time deadline feasibility, showstoppers), fixed-point conversion feedback (Q-format, precision analysis, error bounds), real-time deadline assessment (worst-case execution time, jitter), porting support, and a reusability assessment of PoC firmware. Grounded in IOT_EMBEDDED_SYSTEMS_RESEARCHER_SKILL §6.4 and FIRMWARE_ENGINEER_SKILL §6.9. A novel algorithm outside the precedented surface escalates ESC-NOV; binding production-firmware changes route through ARCH↔FW-001 (ADR).

research_algorithm_transfer.description: RES→FW: algorithm spec, PoC firmware, scientific rationale, preprocessing spec (≥4 weeks before implementation start).

firmware_feasibility.description: FW→RES: feasibility verdict, estimated resources, peripheral/RTOS/timing analysis, fixed-point feedback, reusability.

unit.description: Explicit unit, e.g., KB, cycles, µs, weeks, LSB.

x-macp.tier_rationale: Routine firmware-feasibility assessment and PoC reusability review for research algorithms is agent-autonomous (feasibility within 15 business days; reusability within 10 business days). A novel algorithm/methodology outside the precedented surface escalates ESC-NOV; binding production-firmware adoption routes through ARCH↔FW-001 (ADR).
x-macp.cadence: TRIGGER + CALENDAR (algorithm-spec handoff ≥4 weeks before implementation; feasibility within 15 business days; reusability within 10 business days; bi-weekly joint review during implementation; early notification within 5 business days; annual Research-Firmware Technology Scan, first Tuesday of November)
confirm_conditions: the algorithm spec carries a math description and (for transfer) a Python reference + test vectors
estimated/expected resources and timing (Flash/SRAM/CPU/WCET/jitter/error bound) carry explicit units
the feasibility verdict is stated; INFEASIBLE enumerates the showstoppers
fixed-point conversion feedback carries a Q-format and a bounded error
reject_conditions: a resource, timing, or error-bound quantity emitted without a unit (units rule §3.10)
a research algorithm presented as production-ready firmware without the ARCH↔FW-001 contract/ADR (Contract-First §10.2)
a feasibility verdict of FEASIBLE asserted while real-time deadlines are not met (Honesty Over Polish §10.3)
counter_conditions: ALWAYS escalate ESC-NOV when the algorithm/sensing modality is outside the precedented surface (novelty > 0.80) — propose, do not auto-confirm
a floating-point algorithm lacks fixed-point guidance — request Q-format recommendations and error bounds before implementation
